name: cache
detail: Configure a flow cache parameter for a flow monitor.
syntax: cache {timeout {active | inactive | update} seconds | type {normal | permanent}}

params.name: timeout
params.description: Specifies the flow timeout.

params.name: active
params.description: Specifies the active flow timeout.

params.name: inactive
params.description: Specifies the inactive flow timeout.

params.name: update
params.description: Specifies the update timeout for a permanent flow cache.

params.name: seconds
params.description: The timeout value in seconds. The range is 30 to 604800 (7 days) for a normal flow cache. For a permanent flow cache the range is 1 to 604800 (7 days).

params.name: type
params.description: Specifies the type of the flow cache.

params.name: normal
params.description: Configures a normal cache type. The entries in the flow cache will be aged out according to the timeout active seconds and timeout inactive seconds settings. This is the default cache type.

params.name: permanent
params.description: Configures a permanent cache type. This cache type disables flow removal from the flow cache.

usageSummary: Each flow monitor has a cache that it uses to store all the flows it monitors.  Each cache has various configurable elements, such as the time that a flow is allowed to remain in it.  When a flow times out, it is removed from the cache and sent to any exporters that are configured for the corresponding flow monitor.

name: clear flow exporter
detail: Clear the statistics for a Flexible Netflow flow exporter.

params.name: name
params.description: (Optional) Specifies the name of a flow exporter.

params.name: exporter-name
params.description: (Optional) Name of a flow exporter that was previously configured.

params.name: statistics
params.description: Clears the flow exporter statistics.

usageSummary: The clear flow exporter command removes all statistics from the flow exporter.  These statistics will not be exported and the data gathered in the cache will be lost.  You can view the flow exporter statistics by using the show flow exporter statistics privileged EXEC command.

name: clear flow monitor
detail: Clear a flow monitor cache or flow monitor statistics and to force the export of the data in the flow monitor cache.
syntax: clear flow monitor [name] monitor-name [{[cache] force-export | statistics}]

params.name: name
params.description: Specifies the name of a flow monitor.

params.name: monitor-name
params.description: Name of a flow monitor that was previously configured.

params.name: cache
params.description: (Optional) Clears the flow monitor cache information.

params.name: force-export
params.description: (Optional) Forces the export of the flow monitor cache statistics.

params.name: statistics
params.description: (Optional) Clears the flow monitor statistics.

usageSummary: The clear flow monitor cache command removes all entries from the flow monitor cache.  These entries will not be exported and the data gathered in the cache will be lost.

name: collect
detail: Configure non-key fields for the flow monitor record and to enable capturing the values in the fields for the flow created with the record.

params.name: counter
params.description: Configures the number of bytes or packets in a flow as a non-key field for a flow record. For more information, see collect counter, on page 476.

params.name: interface
params.description: Configures the input and output interface name as a non-key field for a flow record. For more information, see collect interface, on page 477.

params.name: timestamp
params.description: Configures the absolute time of the first seen or last seen packet in a flow as a non-key field for a flow record. For more information, see collect timestamp absolute, on page 478.

params.name: transport
params.description: Enables the collecting of transport TCP flags from a flow record. For more information, see collect transport tcp flags, on page 479.

usageSummary: The values in non-key fields are added to flows to provide additional information about the traffic in the flows.  A change in the value of a non-key field does not create a new flow.  In most cases, the values for non-key fields are taken from only the first packet in the flow.

name: collect counter
detail: Configure the number of bytes or packets in a flow as a non-key field for a flow record.
syntax: collect counter {bytes layer2 long | bytes long | packets long}
noForm: no collect counter {bytes layer2 long | bytes long | packets long}

params.name: bytes layer2 long
params.description: Configures the number of Layer 2 bytes seen in a flow as a non-key field, and enables collecting the total number of Layer 2 bytes from the flow using a 64-bit counter.

params.name: bytes long
params.description: Configures the number of bytes seen in a flow as a non-key field, and enables collecting the total number of bytes from the flow using a 64-bit counter.

params.name: packets long
params.description: Configures the number of packets seen in a flow as a non-key field and enables collecting the total number of packets from the flow using a 64-bit counter.

usageSummary: The collect counter bytes long command configures a 64-bit counter for the number of bytes seen in a flow.  The collect counter packets long command configures a 64-bit counter that will be incremented for each packet seen in the flow.  It is unlikely that a 64-bit counter will ever restart at 0.

name: collect interface
detail: Configure the input and output interface name as a non-key field for a flow record.

params.name: input
params.description: Configures the input interface name as a non-key field and enables collecting the input interface from the flows.

params.name: output
params.description: Configures the output interface name as a non-key field and enables collecting the output interface from the flows.

usageSummary: The Flexible NetFlow collect commands are used to configure non-key fields for the flow monitor record and to enable capturing the values in the fields for the flow created with the record.  The values in non-key fields are added to flows to provide additional information about the traffic in the flows.  A change in the value of a non-key field does not create a new flow.

name: collect timestamp absolute
detail: Configure the absolute time of the first seen or last seen packet in a flow as a non-key field for a flow record.

params.name: first
params.description: Configures the absolute time of the first seen packet in a flow as a non-key field and enables collecting time stamps from the flows.

params.name: last
params.description: Configures the absolute time of the last seen packet in a flow as a non-key field and enables collecting time stamps from the flows.

usageSummary: The collect commands are used to configure non-key fields for the flow monitor record and to enable capturing the values in the fields for the flow created with the record.  The values in non-key fields are added to flows to provide additional information about the traffic in the flows.  A change in the value of a non-key field does not create a new flow.

name: collect transport tcp flags
detail: Enable the collecting of transport TCP flags from a flow.
usageSummary: The values of the transport layer fields are taken from all packets in the flow.  You cannot specify which TCP flag to collect.  You can only specify to collect transport TCP flags.

name: datalink flow monitor

noForm: no datalink flow monitor monitor-name {input | output | sampler sampler-name}

params.name: monitor-name
params.description: Name of the flow monitor to apply to the interface.

params.name: sampler sampler-name
params.description: Enables the specified flow sampler for the flow monitor.

params.name: input
params.description: Monitors traffic that the switch receives on the interface.

params.name: output
params.description: Monitors traffic that the switch sends on the interface.

usageSummary: Before you apply a flow monitor to an interface with the datalink flow monitor command, you must have already created the flow monitor using the flow monitor global configuration command and the flow sampler using the sampler global configuration command.  To enable a flow sampler for the flow monitor, you must have already created the sampler.

params.name: cache

params.name: error

params.name: name

params.name: sampler-name

params.name: sampling samples

name: description
detail: Configure a description for a flow monitor, flow exporter, or flow record.

params.name: description
params.description: Text string that describes the flow monitor, flow exporter, or flow record.

modes: The following command modes are supported:
usageSummary: To return this command to its default setting, use the no description or default description command in the appropriate configuration mode.  The following example configures a description for a flow monitor: Device(config)# flow monitor FLOW-MONITOR-1 Device(config-flow-monitor)# description Monitors traffic to 172. 16.

name: destination
detail: Configure an export destination for a flow exporter.

params.name: hostname
params.description: Hostname of the device to which you want to send the NetFlow information.

params.name: ip-address
params.description: IPv4 address of the workstation to which you want to send the NetFlow information.

params.name: vrf
params.description: (Optional) Specifies that the export data packets are to be sent to the named Virtual Private Network (VPN) routing and forwarding (VRF) instance for routing to the destination, instead of to the global routing table.

params.name: vrf-label
params.description: Name of the VRF instance.

usageSummary: Each flow exporter can have only one destination address or hostname.  When you configure a hostname instead of the IP address for the device, the hostname is resolved immediately and the IPv4 address is stored in the running configuration.  If the hostname-to-IP-address mapping that was used for the original Domain Name System (DNS) name resolution changes dynamically on the DNS server, the device does not detect this, and the exported data continues to be sent to the original IP address, resulting in a loss of data.

name: dscp
detail: Configure a differentiated services code point (DSCP) value for flow exporter datagrams.

params.name: dscp
params.description: DSCP to be used in the DSCP field in exported datagrams. The range is 0 to 63. The default is 0.

usageSummary: To return this command to its default setting, use the no dscp or default dscp flow exporter configuration command.  The following example sets 22 as the value of the DSCP field in exported datagrams: Device(config)# flow exporter FLOW-EXPORTER-1 Device(config-flow-exporter)# dscp 22 Command Reference, Cisco IOS XE Gibraltar 16. 12.

name: export-protocol netflow-v9
detail: Configure NetFlow Version 9 export as the export protocol for a Flexible NetFlow exporter.
usageSummary: The device does not support NetFlow v5 export format, only NetFlow v9 export format is supported.  The following example configures NetFlow Version 9 export as the export protocol for a NetFlow exporter: Device(config)# flow exporter FLOW-EXPORTER-1 Device(config-flow-exporter)# export-protocol netflow-v9 Command Reference, Cisco IOS XE Gibraltar 16. 12.

name: exporter

params.name: exporter-name
params.description: Name of a flow exporter that was previously configured.

To return this command to its default settings, use the no exporter or default exporter flow monitor configuration command.

name: flow exporter

params.name: exporter-name
params.description: Name of the flow exporter that is being created or modified.

usageSummary: Flow exporters export the data in the flow monitor cache to a remote system, such as a server running NetFlow collector, for analysis and storage.  Flow exporters are created as separate entities in the configuration.  Flow exporters are assigned to flow monitors to provide data export capability for the flow monitors.

name: flow monitor
detail: Create a flow monitor, or to modify an existing flow monitor, and enter flow monitor configuration mode.

params.name: monitor-name
params.description: Name of the flow monitor that is being created or modified.

usageSummary: Flow monitors are the Flexible NetFlow component that is applied to interfaces to perform network traffic monitoring.  Flow monitors consist of a flow record and a cache.  You add the record to the flow monitor after you create the flow monitor.

name: flow record

params.name: record-name
params.description: Name of the flow record that is being created or modified.

usageSummary: A flow record defines the keys that Flexible NetFlow uses to identify packets in the flow, as well as other fields of interest that Flexible NetFlow gathers for the flow.  You can define a flow record with any combination of keys and fields of interest.  The supports a rich set of keys.

name: ip flow monitor

noForm: no ip flow monitor monitor-name [sampler sampler-name] {input | output}

params.name: monitor-name
params.description: Name of the flow monitor to apply to the interface.

params.name: sampler sampler-name
params.description: (Optional) Enables the specified flow sampler for the flow monitor.

params.name: input
params.description: Monitors IPv4 traffic that the device receives on the interface.

params.name: output
params.description: Monitors IPv4 traffic that the device transmits on the interface.

usageSummary: Before you can apply a flow monitor to an interface with the ip flow monitor command, you must have already created the flow monitor using the flow monitor global configuration command.  When you add a sampler to a flow monitor, only packets that are selected by the named sampler will be entered into the cache to form flows.  Each use of a sampler causes separate statistics to be stored for that usage.

params.name: record-name
params.description: Name of a user-defined flow record that was previously configured.

usageSummary: Each flow monitor requires a record to define the contents and layout of its cache entries.  The flow monitor can use one of the wide range of predefined record formats, or advanced users may create their own record formats.

name: sampler
detail: Create a Flexible NetFlow flow sampler, or to modify an existing Flexible NetFlow flow sampler, and to enter Flexible NetFlow sampler configuration mode.

params.name: sampler-name
params.description: Name of the flow sampler that is being created or modified.

usageSummary: Flow samplers are used to reduce the load placed by Flexible NetFlow on the networking device to monitor traffic by limiting the number of packets that are analyzed.  You configure a rate of sampling that is 1 out of a range of 2-1024 packets.  Flow samplers are applied to interfaces in conjunction with a flow monitor to implement sampled Flexible NetFlow.

name: show flow exporter
detail: Display flow exporter status and statistics.
syntax: show flow exporter [{broker [{detail | picture}] | export-ids netflow-v9 | [name] exporter-name [{statistics | templates}] | statistics | templates}]

params.name: broker
params.description: (Optional) Displays information about the state of the broker for the Flexible NetFlow flow exporter.

params.name: detail
params.description: (Optional) Displays detailed information about the flow exporter broker.

params.name: picture
params.description: (Optional) Displays a picture of the broker state.

params.name: export-ids netflow-v9
params.description: (Optional) Displays the NetFlow Version 9 export fields that can be exported and their IDs.

params.name: name
params.description: (Optional) Specifies the name of a flow exporter.

params.name: exporter-name
params.description: (Optional) Name of a flow exporter that was previously configured.

params.name: statistics
params.description: (Optional) Displays statistics for all flow exporters or for the specified flow exporter.

params.name: templates
params.description: (Optional) Displays template information for all flow exporters or for the specified flow exporter.

name: show flow interface
detail: Display the Flexible NetFlow configuration and status for an interface.

params.name: type
params.description: (Optional) The type of interface on which you want to display Flexible NetFlow accounting configuration information.

params.name: number
params.description: (Optional) The number of the interface on which you want to display Flexible NetFlow accounting configuration information.

name: show flow monitor
detail: Display the status and statistics for a Flexible NetFlow flow monitor.
syntax: show flow monitor [{broker [{detail | picture}] | [name] monitor-name [{cache [format {csv | record | table} | aggregate | filter | sort]}] | provisioning | statistics}]

params.name: broker
params.description: (Optional) Displays information about the state of the broker for the flow monitor

params.name: detail
params.description: (Optional) Displays detailed information about the flow monitor broker.

params.name: picture
params.description: (Optional) Displays a picture of the broker state.

params.name: name
params.description: (Optional) Specifies the name of a flow monitor.

params.name: monitor-name
params.description: (Optional) Name of a flow monitor that was previously configured.

params.name: cache
params.description: (Optional) Displays the contents of the cache for the flow monitor.

params.name: format
params.description: (Optional) Specifies the use of one of the format options for formatting the display output.

params.name: aggregate
params.description: (Optional) Displays an aggregate of the given fields.

params.name: filter
params.description: (Optional) Filters and displays only matching flow records.

params.name: sort
params.description: (Optional) Sorts the resulting flow records in the required order.

params.name: csv
params.description: (Optional) Displays the flow monitor cache contents in comma-separated variables (CSV) format.

params.name: record
params.description: (Optional) Displays the flow monitor cache contents in record format.

params.name: table
params.description: (Optional) Displays the flow monitor cache contents in table format.

params.name: provisioning
params.description: (Optional) Displays the flow monitor provisioning information.

params.name: statistics
params.description: (Optional) Displays the statistics for the flow monitor.

usageSummary: The cache keyword uses the record format by default.  The uppercase field names in the display output of the show flowmonitor monitor-name cache command are key fields that Flexible NetFlow uses to differentiate flows.  The lowercase field names in the display output of the show flow monitor monitor-name cache command are nonkey fields from which Flexible NetFlow collects values as additional data for the cache.

name: source
detail: Configure the source IP address interface for all of the packets sent by a Flexible NetFlow flow exporter.

params.name: interface-type
params.description: Type of interface whose IP address you want to use for the source IP address of the packets sent by a Flexible NetFlow flow exporter.

params.name: interface-number
params.description: Interface number whose IP address you want to use for the source IP address of the packets sent by a Flexible NetFlow flow exporter.

usageSummary: The benefits of using a consistent IP source address for the datagrams that Flexible NetFlow sends include the following: • The source IP address of the datagrams exported by Flexible NetFlow is used by the destination system to determine from which device the Flexible NetFlow data is arriving.  If your network has two or more paths that can be used to send Flexible NetFlow datagrams from the device to the destination system and you do not specify the source interface from which the source IP address is to be obtained, the device uses the IP address of the interface over which the datagram is transmitted as the source IP address of the datagram.  In this situation the destination system might receive Flexible NetFlow datagrams from the same device, but with different source IP addresses.

name: template data timeout
detail: Specify a timeout period for resending flow exporter template data.

params.name: seconds
params.description: Timeout value in seconds. The range is 1 to 86400. The default is 600.

usageSummary: Flow exporter template data describes the exported data records.  Data records cannot be decoded without the corresponding template.  The template data timeout command controls how often those templates are exported.

name: transport
detail: Configure the transport protocol for a flow exporter for Flexible NetFlow.

params.name: udp udp-port
params.description: Specifies User Datagram Protocol (UDP) as the transport protocol and the UDP port number.

usageSummary: To return this command to its default settings, use the no transport or default transport flow exporter configuration command.  The following example configures UDP as the transport protocol and a UDP port number of 250: Device(config)# flow exporter FLOW-EXPORTER-1 Device(config-flow-exporter)# transport udp 250 Command Reference, Cisco IOS XE Gibraltar 16. 12.

name: ttl
detail: Configure the time-to-live (TTL) value.

params.name: ttl
params.description: Time-to-live (TTL) value for exported datagrams. The range is 1 to 255. The default is 255.

usageSummary: To return this command to its default settings, use the no ttl or default ttl flow exporter configuration command.  The following example specifies a TTL of 15: Device(config)# flow exporter FLOW-EXPORTER-1 Device(config-flow-exporter)# ttl 15 Command Reference, Cisco IOS XE Gibraltar 16. 12.
